Continental._comment: Bangalore site, three counters (South Indian, North Indian, Pan Asian). Only the South Indian counter is configured here; the other two keep the city ruleset untouched. The client name is the KEY, not the filename — the loader reads the directory and matches `clients.name` byte for byte, so a mismatch loads zero rules and still returns a plausible plan.

rules._comment: 'Flavoured rice on mon wed fri. Which flavour rice no white rice, and vice versa.' Two day-restrictions whose weekday lists are exact COMPLEMENTS over the five working days, which is the shape Corning Chakan, Amadeus Pune, Gartner, Ikea and Stryker NCR already use. Not a mutual exclusion between the two slots: a complementary pair can never both drop and leave a day with no rice at all. The days are FIXED rather than solver-chosen because `white_rice` is a stamped constant (src/constants.py CONST_SLOTS), not a candidate the solver picks, so nothing in the model could trade one against the other. Before this both slots ran every day — a real solve served a flavoured rice AND steamed rice on all five.
rules.name: continental_south_flavoured_rice_mon_wed_fri

rules._comment: The 'vice versa' half: white rice on exactly the two days the flavoured-rice slot stands down. Written as its own weekday list rather than derived from the rule above, because a constant slot is stamped AFTER the solve and has no cell to key off — a `slot_day_restriction` on a const slot used to be a silent no-op and the staple appeared every day anyway (`menu_solver._rows_to_week_plan` now honours skip_cells for them). The site works Mon-Fri, so the two lists must union to all five or a day comes out with no rice at all; if the flavoured-rice days change, this list changes with them.
rules.name: continental_south_white_rice_tue_thu
